title: Elench: A Cost-Contract Language and Static Verification Framework for AI-Generated Code
description:
Elench is a programming language designed for AI code generation. Instead of asking whether generated code is correct, it asks whether the generated code's cost stays inside a declared contract.

  • Every function carries a cost signature derived by static analysis over a symbolic value domain (target { time: { max: O(...) } }).
  • Multiple candidates for the same task are declared with choose over a closed set; the toolchain computes where they cross over and dispatches by input size (?!label(...)).
  • Static estimates and measured timings are kept in separate metrics with explicit cost.source / cost.semantics attributes, and conflicts are resolved in favour of measurement.
  • The whole toolchain emits machine-readable cost signatures (dsh cost --signature) so an agent can treat cost as a budget prior rather than an afterthought.

The repository contains the language specification, a Python reference implementation (lexer, parser, formatter, checker, type checker, two value domains, cost analysis, dispatch planning, OTLP exporter), 30 test suites with 633 assertions, and ten hand-written sample programs.
